stories.title: €23m spent on Assessment of Need challenges since 2021
stories.summary: The State has spent over €23 million in legal costs arising from Assessments of Need (AON) challenges since 2021, new figures have revealed. Under the Disability Act 2005, parents can take a case against the HSE if they do not receive an assessment report for their child with special needs within a six-month timeframe, if they are unhappy with the outcome of the assessment or if they feel the service was below par. An AON is a formal legal process carried out by the HSE to identify a child's health and educational needs stemming from a disability, and to determine the appropriate public services required to meet those needs. However, there are too few specialists in the system and lengthy waiting lists have become the norm.

stories.title: New anti-money laundering rules target gambling industry
stories.summary: New anti-money laundering rules are set to be introduced as part of a wide-reaching nationwide crackdown. The Government is aiming to target attempts by criminal gangs and terrorist organisations to legitimise money through the gambling industry, cryptocurrencies and other routes. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris will announce the rules as part of Ireland's first national anti-money laundering strategy, saying the changes will send the message that Ireland will "not be a safe place to launder criminal proceeds". The strategy, which builds on plans announced earlier this year, is intended to help strengthen Ireland's defences against money laundering, terrorist financing and other areas of criminality.

stories.title: I-RES sees slight revenue increase, profits jump
stories.summary: Ireland's largest private landlord, Irish Residential Properties REIT (I-RES) has posted its interim results for the first half of the year, saying strong operational and strategic delivery drove earning growth and shareholder returns. The company saw a slight increase in its revenues year on year - it booked €43.1m euro in the six month period, up 1.1 percent on the same period of last year. The group posted a profit before tax of €48 million versus €16.3 million in the prior period. It said this was driven by the non-cash fair value movement of its assets which was underpinned by performance of the portfolio and stable yields.

stories.title: Bones of medieval kings saved from Spanish wildfire
stories.summary: Firefighters raced to save a mythical 1,000-year-old monastery in northeastern Spain as a growing wildfire prompted the hasty removal of the bones of the medieval monarchs buried there. The blaze broke out earlier this week and yesterday bore down on two monasteries of San Juan de la Peña, a symbol of the Aragon region, perched in mountainous, rugged terrain. The oldest monastery, linked by legend to the Holy Grail, has origins in the 10th century and holds the remains of the first kings of the medieval kingdom of Aragon. The army's emergencies unit (UME) released footage of its officers rushing to remove the monastery's priceless treasures yesterday, including transparent boxes full of skulls and bones, artwork and a chalice, as flames licked the surrounding hills.

stories.summary: Fortune fell on Derry City's side as goals from Michael Duffy and new signing Tyler Smith saw the visitors to a hard-fought 2-1 victory over UCD to advance to the Club Orange FAI Cup fourth round. The attackers struck in either half, bisected by a superb Louis Dignam equaliser, in a game the Students dominated for long spells and hit the woodwork no fewer than three times. Duffy had found the net with an early free kick as the Premier Division side looked set to coast past their less experienced counterparts. What followed was far from a fait accomplis however, as the Belfield side controlled much of the game with varied passing and patterns of play that bamboozled the visitors.

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.

stories.title: Rangers not ready for Europa, admits McInnes
stories.summary: Derek McInnes admitted Rangers are not yet good enough for top European competition after exiting the Europa League qualifiers with a 3-2 aggregate defeat to Jagiellonia Bialystok. The Light Blues had lost 2-1 in the first leg in Poland last week but captain Lawrence Shankland levelled the tie with a penalty on 19 minutes at Ibrox – only for the visitors to deservedly score in the 65th minute through attacker Nik Prelec for the 1-1 draw which took them through to the play-off. McInnes has not won in four games since taking over as boss in the summer and he described the angry reaction from the Gers fans at full-time as "justified." Rangers, who finished third in the William Hill Premiership last season, reached the Europa League final in 2022 but will take on Jablonec, from the Czech Republic, in the Conference League play-off round.

stories.summary: Luigi Mangione has admitted in court to fatally shooting a US health insurance executive and pleaded guilty to two federal charges of stalking the executive with the intent to kill him. It could also allow him to seek dismissal of state murder charges and delay an upcoming trial in that case. US District Judge Margaret Garnett told Mangione that if he pleaded guilty he could face a maximum sentence of life in prison on each count.

To ease him through his final days, Dr. Josef Alois calls for someone from his past. Enter Catherine Carolan, now an Oxford professor. A novel in two strands, A Thought without Collision is a meditation on how we construct our relationship to the world around us.

stories.title: Strong 7.7 magnitude earthquake hits Indonesia
stories.summary: A strong 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, killing at least two and sending thousands running in panic after authorities issued a tsunami warning. Residents in Nagekeo regency, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated -- a possible sign of an approaching tsunami. The epicentre of the shallow quake was located off the north coast of the island, about 68 kilometres northwest of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said. The initial jolt was followed by strong aftershocks in the same area, including one with a magnitude of 6.1.

stories.title: Counting of votes under way in Clacton by-election
stories.summary:
Counting is under way in the Clacton by-election pitting Reform UK leader Nigel Farage against satirical candidate Count Binface in a vote dismissed by some residents as a "farce". Mr Farage, who triggered the vote by resigning the parliamentary seat he had held since 2024 over an investigation into his finances, is up against Binface and dozens of other fringe candidates in the Clacton constituency of eastern Essex. The vote has been shunned by Britain's main political parties, including the ruling Labour, as a stunt by the Reform UK leader - once touted as a potential prime minister - to dodge scrutiny of his dealings. That has left candidates such as Binface - the alter ego of comedian Jon Harvey - to grab the attention.
Analysts predict a win for Mr Farage - but they also predict an uncomfortably large share of up to 20% of the votes going to the self-styled "intergalactic space warrior" who wears a rubbish bin on his head.

stories.title: Oil set for weekly gains
stories.summary: Oil prices were mixed today but set for weekly gains after the US threatened an indefinite naval blockade of Iran, raising concerns about disruptions to crude supplies from the Middle East. Brent futures were down 12 cents, or 0.1%, to $86.95 a barrel this afternoon, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up 13 cents, or 0.2%, to $81.38 a barrel. Brent and WTI were on track for weekly gains of about 3.4% and 4%, respectively. Higher oil prices are a natural result of the latest approach by the US, which implies little hope of a near-term resolution in the Middle East, said Bjarne Schieldrop, chief analyst for commodities at SEB Research.

stories.title: Shootout delight as Galway squeeze past brave Bray
stories.summary: Galway United progressed to the quarter-final stages of the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup following a hard-fought penalty shoot-out victory over Bray Wanderers at Eamonn Deacy Park. Ahead of the cup encounter, experienced defender Anthony O'Connor, who signed for United during the week, came into the team to make his debut, while Kris Twardek was handed his first start in some time as he makes a return to full fitness. The Seagulls, who are aiming to cement their place in the League of Ireland First Division play-offs, settled well into proceedings, while also showing confidence in possession. The first opportunity of the game was generated by David Hurley when his superb first touch set him up for a left-footed strike which cannoned off the woodwork.

stories.title: McDonald 'couldn't turn down' chance at pro career
stories.summary: Kobe McDonald says he couldn't turn down the opportunity to become a professional athlete in his first interview as a St Kilda player. The 18-year old McDonald, son of former Mayo great Ciaran McDonald, was one of the stories of the inter-county season as he made a rapid adjustment to inter-county football and then helped the county deliver a sensational and unexpected All-Ireland final victory amid euphoric scenes at Croke Park. A further element to the story was the knowledge all the while that McDonald was bound for Aussie Rules, having agreed to join St Kilda once he'd completed his leaving cert, which he did during the summer. "I've always dreamed of being a professional athlete," McDonald told St Kilda's YouTube channel.
